cards.title: Ten minutes. One folder. Less panic.
cards.body: When the doctor asks for last year's report, nobody should be digging through the almirah. A basic system takes one sitting to set up.

cards.title: Minutes 1 to 3: gather everything
cards.body: Prescriptions, reports, discharge papers, scans. From drawers, handbags and the car dashboard. Don't sort yet. Just pile it all in one place.

cards.title: Minutes 4 to 6: one pile per person
cards.body: Mummy, Papa, Dadi, you. Within each pile, put the newest on top. That one step solves most of the searching.

cards.title: Minutes 7 to 8: photograph the important ones
cards.body: Recent prescriptions, latest reports, discharge summaries. Good light, flat on a table. Save them in a phone folder named after each person.

cards.title: Minute 9: one physical file each
cards.body: A cheap clear file per person, labelled with their name. Keep them together in one spot that everyone at home knows.

cards.title: Minute 10: write the medicine list
cards.body: Current medicines, doses and timings on one sheet at the front of each file. Update it whenever a prescription changes.

cards.title: Ten minutes now saves hours later
cards.body: Next hospital visit, you grab one file and go. AICA is building family profiles to keep this on one phone, but paper still counts.

takeaway: Gather, sort by person, photograph key papers, file them and add a current medicine list: ten minutes for a calmer family.
share: Sort the family's health papers in 10 minutes. One file per person, newest on top.
